newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-PARIS SAINT-GERMAIN PREVENT MORE TURKISH DELIGHT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PARIS SAINT-GERMAIN PREVENT MORE TURKISH DELIGHT.

text.p: Brazil's Leonardo inspired Cup Winners' Cup holders Paris Saint-Germain on Thursday as they ended Turkish hopes of a second triumph in Europe within 24 hours.
Midfielder Leonardo scored one goal and set up two more to fire PSG to a 4-0 second-round second-leg win over Galatasaray in Paris, putting the French team in the quarter-finals 6-4 on aggregate.

Norway's Brann Bergen, who surprised Dutch opponents PSV Eindhoven, and England's Liverpool, who hit three goals in six minutes after being rattled by Sion of Switzerland, were among other sides to secure last-eight places.
With a 4-2 lead from the first leg, Galatasaray had their sights on an overall victory to share the European spotlight with fellow Turks Fenerbahce.
Fenerbahce beat Manchester United 1-0 in the Champions' League on Wednesday, ending the English club's proud 40-year unbeaten home record in European competition.

However, PSG soon stamped their authority on the game, with Leonardo opening the scoring in the ninth minute and Panama striker Dely Valdes adding a second from a free kick by the Brazilian after 23 minutes.
The industrious Leonardo also provided a low cross which France striker Patrice Loko turned home for the third goal and PSG's other Brazilian Rai struck the fourth.
Rai said: "The way we reacted is just fabulous. It means that we will live more great nights like this one. It's wonderful for our fans and for us too."

A large contingent of Turkish supporters in the 34,000 crowd threw coins and seats on to the pitch after striker Hakan Sukur was denied a penalty 13 minutes from time, but there was no further trouble.
Brann Bergen drew 2-2 at PSV to reach the quarter-finals 4-3 on aggregate after the Dutch side failed to make the most of a spate of chances.
Geir Hasund scored in the 35th minute from a cross by Tore Andre Flo, who got the second himself in the 59th to put the Norwegians on course for success.

Rene Eykelkamp and Boudewijn Zenden replied for PSV in the second half, but it was too little too late for the Dutch league leaders, who ironically have scored 15 goals in their last two home league matches.

A three-goal burst in six minutes by John Barnes and Robbie Fowler spared Liverpool's blushes against Sion, the English team winning the second leg clash at Anfield 6-3 to go through 8-4 on aggregate.

Liverpool trailed 3-2 at one stage and, though the aggregate score was then 4-4, they were in jeopardy of losing on the away goals rule until Barnes and Fowler, who struck two goals in a minute, transformed the whole shape of the tie.
Frenchman Cyril Jeunechamp, nicknamed "the bull from Nimes", was sent off after trying to attack the refreee in the second leg against AIK Stockholm in Sweden.
The incident happened five minutes before the end of the match in which French third division side Nimes beat AIK 1-0, although the Swedish team reached the quarter-finals 3-2 on aggregate.

Nimes were growing frustrated at being unable to turn their domination into more goals when midfielder Jeunechamp felt he was robbed of a free kick after being brought down by AIK striker Pascal Simpson.

The Frenchman went after Slovakian referee Lubos Michel, raised his foot in an attempt to kick the official but was held back by team mates. Jeunechamp, who had been shown a yellow card a few minutes earlier, was sent off.
Paris Saint-Germain, Brann Bergen, Liverpool and AIK Stockholm were joined in the quarter-finals by Barcelona, Italy's Fiorentina, Benfica of Portugal and AEK Athens.
